title: Attention Is All You Need
abstract: We propose the Transformer, a sequence transduction architecture that relies entirely on attention mechanisms and dispenses with recurrence and convolutions. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show the models are higher in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. The approach also generalizes to English constituency parsing, achieving competitive results.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
abstract: We introduce BERT, a language representation model that pre-trains deep bidirectional transformers on unlabeled text by conditioning on both left and right context. The pre-trained model can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer for many tasks. BERT obtains new state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks, including question answering and language inference.

title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
abstract: We present a replication study of BERT pretraining that carefully measures the impact of key hyperparameters and training data size. We find that BERT was significantly undertrained and can match or exceed the performance of models published after it. Our best model achieves state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks, which shows that design choices in pretraining matter.

title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
abstract: We introduce a unified framework that converts every language problem into a text-to-text format and systematically compare pre-training objectives, architectures and datasets. We train large transformer models on a cleaned web corpus. Combining these insights with scale, we obtain state-of-the-art results on summarization, question answering and text classification benchmarks.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
abstract: We train GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, and test it in the few-shot setting without any gradient updates. GPT-3 achieves strong performance on many NLP datasets, including translation and question answering, from only a handful of examples in the prompt. We also find that it struggles on some datasets and discuss broader societal impacts.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
abstract: We present retrieval-augmented generation, which combines a pre-trained sequence-to-sequence model with a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed through a neural retriever. The approach lets a language model draw on external, updatable knowledge. Our models set the state of the art on several open-domain question answering tasks and generate more specific and factual text than parametric-only baselines.

title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
abstract: We apply a standard transformer directly to sequences of image patches for image classification, without relying on convolutional networks. When pre-trained on large datasets, the Vision Transformer attains excellent results compared to state-of-the-art convolutional networks while requiring substantially fewer computational resources to train.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract: We explore how generating a chain of thought, a series of intermediate reasoning steps, improves the ability of large language models to perform complex reasoning. We show that including a few chain-of-thought exemplars in the prompt lets sufficiently large models solve arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning tasks. A prompted model achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on a math word problem benchmark.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
abstract: Making language models larger does not make them better at following user intent. We fine-tune GPT-3 using supervised learning on labeler demonstrations and then reinforcement learning from human feedback. In human evaluations, outputs from a much smaller fine-tuned model are preferred to outputs from the much larger GPT-3, with improvements in truthfulness and reductions in toxic output.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
abstract: We introduce LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters, trained on trillions of tokens using exclusively publicly available datasets. We show that LLaMA-13B outperforms GPT-3 on most benchmarks despite being more than ten times smaller, and that the largest model is competitive with the best existing models.
